shortcut_explanation: 5/8 is 0.625, a little more than 0.6.
full_explanation: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625 and 0.625 > 0.600, so Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: a% of b always equals b% of a. Both are 20 × 45 ÷ 100.
full_explanation: 20% of 45 = 20 × 45 / 100 and 45% of 20 = 45 × 20 / 100. Multiplication does not care about order, so both equal 9.

shortcut_explanation: 2³ = 8 and 3² = 9, so B wins by one.
full_explanation: 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 and 3² = 3 × 3 = 9. Since 8 < 9, Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: The 10 is far above 5 and the 3 is only a little below, so the average is pulled above 5.
full_explanation: The sum is 18 and 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Since 6 > 5, Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Exponents before the minus sign. A is +16 and B is −16.
full_explanation: In (−2)⁴ the brackets make −2 the base, and an even power of a negative is positive: 16. In −2⁴ the exponent is done first, 2⁴ = 16, and then the minus sign makes it −16. 16 > −16.

shortcut_explanation: The √ sign means the non-negative root, so √25 is exactly 5, not ±5.
full_explanation: Both 5 and −5 square to 25, but the symbol √25 names only the non-negative one, 5. So the quantities are equal.
(50 − 1)(50 + 1) = 50² − 1² = 2500 − 1 = 2499, and 2499 < 2500. Two numbers with the same sum have the largest product when they are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Test a positive and a negative. x = 1 makes B bigger, x = −1 makes A bigger.
full_explanation: 2x − x = x. When x > 0, 2x is greater; when x < 0, x is greater; when x = 0 they are equal. The relation depends on x.

shortcut_explanation: Try x = 2: 8 beats 4. Try x = ½: ⅛ loses to ¼. Two different results, so D.
full_explanation: x³ − x² = x²(x − 1). With x > 0, x² is positive, so the sign depends on x − 1: A is greater when x > 1, B when 0 < x < 1, and they are equal at x = 1.

shortcut_explanation: y has 3 parts and x has 2 parts of the same positive size, so y is bigger.
full_explanation: x : y = 2 : 3 means y = 3x/2. Since x > 0, 3x/2 − x = x/2 > 0, so y > x.

shortcut_explanation: |x| is a distance, so it is never negative. Here x is negative, so |x| wins.
full_explanation: For x < 0, |x| = −x, which is positive, while x itself is negative. Every positive number is greater than every negative number.

shortcut_explanation: (x + 1)² is x² + 2x + 1, so subtracting 1 leaves x² + 2x. That is exactly x(x + 2).
full_explanation: x(x + 2) = x² + 2x and (x + 1)² − 1 = x² + 2x + 1 − 1 = x² + 2x. The two expressions are the same for every x.

shortcut_explanation: √ gives the non-negative root, so √(x²) undoes the sign as well as the square. That is exactly what |x| does.
full_explanation: x² is the same for x and −x, and √ returns the non-negative number with that square. That number is |x|, so √(x²) = |x| for every real x. Test x = −3: √9 = 3 = |−3|.

shortcut_explanation: Nothing says x is a whole number. x = 4.5 and x = 3.5 both fit, so D.
full_explanation: If x had to be an integer it would be 4 and the answer would be C. But x can be any number between 3 and 5: 4.5 > 4 and 3.5 < 4.

shortcut_explanation: Multiplying both sides by −1 flips an inequality. a > b becomes −a < −b.
full_explanation: From a > b, subtract a + b from both sides: −b > −a. This holds whatever the signs of a and b, so −b is always greater.

shortcut_explanation: The two short sides must add up to more than the long side. So 3 + x > 7, which means x > 4.
full_explanation: In any triangle each side is less than the sum of the other two. 7 < 3 + x gives x > 4, and x < 3 + 7 gives x < 10. Every possible x is greater than 4.

shortcut_explanation: x/y is bigger than 1. Adding the same amount to top and bottom pulls a fraction toward 1, so it shrinks. Check x = 2, y = 1: 3/2 is less than 2.
full_explanation: Both denominators are positive, so compare by cross-multiplying: (x + 1)y versus x(y + 1), that is xy + y versus xy + x. Since y < x, the left side is smaller, so (x + 1)/(y + 1) < x/y.

shortcut_explanation: An even power hides the sign: x could be 3 or −3. One gives equal, the other makes B bigger, so D.
full_explanation: x² = 9 has two solutions, x = 3 and x = −3. At x = 3 the quantities are equal; at x = −3, Quantity B is greater. The relation is not fixed.

shortcut_explanation: Each pair of −1s multiplies to +1, and an odd count leaves one −1 over. So (−1)ⁿ is −1 every time.
full_explanation: Write n = 2k + 1. Then (−1)ⁿ = ((−1)²)ᵏ × (−1) = 1ᵏ × (−1) = −1. This holds for negative odd n too, since (−1)⁻¹ = −1. The quantities are always equal.

shortcut_explanation: Both are negative and x is further from 0. Squaring turns distance from 0 into size, so x² wins. Check x = −3, y = −2: 9 beats 4.
full_explanation: x < y < 0 means |x| > |y| > 0. Squares of non-negative numbers keep their order, so x² = |x|² > |y|² = y².
